title: Useless and unhelpful
body:
I had high hopes for Goblin Tools as someone with ADHD, but this app has been a major letdown. The features are either overly simplistic or completely broken. The to-do list is no better than a basic app like Google Keep, and the other tools are clunky and unreliable. The time estimator is especially ridiculous—it gave me results like washing a car in 2 seconds, flying to Japan in 30 minutes, and washing dishes in 3 seconds. It’s worse than useless.

The UX/UI design is also not ADHD-friendly at all—it feels chaotic, unclear, and not thoughtfully structured for neurodivergent users. Honestly, you’re better off asking ChatGPT or Gemini for help with tasks or time estimates—they’re more accurate and free. I regret paying for this app and can’t recommend it.

I do hope that there will be an option to provide writing prompts/instructions to generate text some day, but as a thoroughly neurospicy person, goblin is absolutely invaluable. Can’t wait for teacher tools to fully launch!

title: Best App Ever
body:
My friend recommended and told me about this app that in turn had been recommended by her therapist. 
I don’t have ADHD or similar conditions, but I do have health conditions that make it difficult for me to get things done if at all in a timely manner. 

This app in the few days I have had it,  has changed my life in the way it breaks tasks down into manageable chunks so I have been able to get long outstanding jobs done. The cluttered cork board for example that had paperwork that was 3 years old. The dirty window and window ledge. The app doesn’t judge but enables. By splitting the cleaning of these down into 3 separate jobs  I have now been able to get it done. The cleaning caddy will be next. I daren’t think what grime is in there but I know by letting the app break the task up, I WILL get it done. 

Well done to the Developer.

title: My goblin brain thanks you!
body:
I have ADHD and came across the web application for Goblin Tools on forums.
The mobile app is magic! It’s built beautifully and gives me all the tools I need in my pocket ☺️ 

The fact it isn’t subscription based is also incredibly helpful - I know it’s mine and can use it whenever I need, without having to worry about whether it’s “worth it” each month or if I’m going to forget to cancel! 

The “unwaffle” feature in the formalizer tool is my favourite - brevity isn’t a strong suit of mine (as you can see from above) and in my job, I have written far too many lengthy emails that don’t clearly articulate my point, or overwhelm people. I’ve used the formaliser to speak to my boss about important matters, share messages with clients and it’s absolute magic! 

I think the best way to demonstrate the value is to show you, so here’s this same review “Formalized” to 4 chillis:

“I love the Goblin Tools mobile app for people with ADHD. It's beautifully built and has all the tools I need in one place. 

Plus, it's not subscription-based, so I don't have to worry about the cost or cancellation. 

The "unwaffle" feature in the formalizer tool is amazing. It helps me cut down on lengthy emails and effectively communicate with my boss and clients. It's absolute magic!”

Thank you for building such a wonderful application - I’ve already gifted it to a friend and would recommend to anyone who needs a little help navigating a neurodiverse existence in a world built for neurotypical brains!

title: Great - but
body:
This app is fabulous. I hope in the future they add a way to order the tasks in a way that reflects how the tasks rely on each other.

This is what I struggle most with - getting tangled at what has to come first since other tasks rely on completion of elements from previous tasks.

Ex: dust piano - but piano can’t be dusted until upstairs is swept since more dust accumulates when sweeping. Upstairs should be swept but actually these dishes should be done first. Do dishes- but dishes can’t be done until sink is cleaned and dishes are collected from all around the house. Dishes shouldn’t be collected until all garbage is cleared but wait is this even garbage? I think this is an unfinished project I should get to quickly first… etc - sos

Untangling this feels like a ball of yarn that a cat plays with, and my house is indifferent to my plight.

author: Express Nebula

title: Where have you been 😭
body:
I could have done with this app or even the web browser version so many years ago… I have been able to easily identify what tasks need to be done and when but, breaking them down and knowing where to start has always been my downfall.
I’ve recently moved and all my stuff is piled up around me. I’ve wanted to clean up and get it all packed away so badly but, I just don’t know where to start. I simply put “finish unpacking” into the magic to-do list and even just the first results, breaking up the tasks made me want to cry. The fact that I can have those sub-tasks broken down even more… I can’t. This is going to help so much, I can feel it. The tasks given are just plain and simple and don’t feel condescending at all which, I really struggle with. Sometimes, having another human try and help or break things down for me makes me feel useless or like they’re treating me like a kid. This removes that and I’m so freaking happy.
Thank you from me personally and my neurospicy brain. Thank you 💜

author: Adonlon

title: Get this app!
body:
OMG I have never bought an app quicker in my life! I watched a review of it on TikTok which instantly caught my attention. 
The reading more in messages, how to word emails so they have the correct tone, even the dreaded what to have for dinner without resorting to a takeaway will never be an issue again!
The breakdown of large tasks is going to be so helpful especially with tickboxes so you can actually focus and not get sidetracked by everything else going on!
The brain dump will also have a huge impact on my sleep as often I get lots of tasks I have to do in my head as I’m drifting off and forget about them when it comes time to actually do them! So of course then I stay up and worry about them so I don’t forget but with the brain dump, all the random thoughts can go in and an actual task list made up from all the jibber jabber appears! Fantastic!
